Traditional Mince Pies

Served at: Fourth Sunday of Advent

Makes 12 mince piesPrep 30 minCook 20 min

Mince pies are a classic British treat traditionally served during the Christmas season, especially on the Fourth Sunday of Advent. These small, sweet pastries filled with spiced mincemeat symbolize the festive spirit and are enjoyed by families as part of holiday celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons cold water
  • 1 1/4 cups (340 g) mincemeat (store-bought or homemade)
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • Powdered sugar, for dusting

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a large bowl, rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
  3. Add the sugar, egg, and cold water, then mix until a dough forms. Wrap in plastic and chill for 15 minutes.
  4. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to about 1/8 inch (3 mm) thickness.
  5. Cut out 12 circles slightly larger than your tart tins for the bases, and 12 smaller circles or stars for the tops.
  6. Press the larger circles into the tart tins and fill each with about 1 tablespoon of mincemeat.
  7. Place the smaller dough shapes on top and press the edges to seal.
  8. Brush the tops with beaten egg.
  9. Bake for 18-20 minutes until golden brown.
  10. Allow to cool slightly, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, use homemade mincemeat made with dried fruits, spices, and a splash of brandy.
  • You can freeze unbaked mince pies for up to one month; bake them straight from the freezer, adding a few extra minutes to the baking time.
  • Serve warm with a dollop of brandy butter or cream for a traditional touch.
